outcome: birth within 2 weeks of ultrasound scan
cohort: 8,977 women with singleton pregnancies without fetal anomalies who underwent an ultrasound scan between 23+0 and 36+6 weeks gestation at a tertiary referral hospital in 2014 and 2015
finding: A low CPR was associated with an increased risk of preterm birth and birth within 2 weeks of the scan, particularly at 28 weeks gestation, but not with spontaneous preterm birth.
mod_finding: Women with a low CPR at 28 weeks gestation had a higher likelihood of emergency cesarean delivery for nonreassuring fetal status.
